traits.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Dichapetalaceae: leaves alternate; leaves simple; margins entire; veins pinnate; stipules present; plants hermaphrodite or monoecious; ovary superior, half inferior or inferior; floral cup absent; stems woody; flowers in cymes; flowers actinomorphic or zygomorphic; perianth sepals and petals; fruit drupe; stamens 3 to 5; carpels 2 to 3 (-4). Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py); a state the authors qualify (rarely, usually, a share) keeps its word, an unqualified one beside a usual state reads as sometimes.

traits.zygomorphy.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data), family Dichapetalaceae: its irregular flowers are of no named kind (pea flower, two lips, orchid lip), read from the coded corolla symmetry (spec-rework/b1/delta): zygomorphy other. Its flowers are not mostly zygomorphic, so a plant of it states its own symmetry; one that is zygomorphic draws this kind, and one stating none is drawn regular.
